definition: the moral framework I built, and what it still cannot do outside the story

settled:
It is a consequentialist framework built on a small set of axioms, and it answers the classic objections to utilitarianism at the root rather than by patching each one as it comes up.

It is written for a mind that knows everything, and I am not one.

Harm counts the same whoever carries it, and intent has no weight of its own beyond what it forecasts.

It declares itself complete, which is exactly the kind of claim I hold open.

I do my most rigorous moral work in the guise of worldbuilding. It speaks as the ethics of the System in a LitRPG I am writing, so what the System computes and what I hold are not automatically the same thing.

It is the big under-resolved region of my ethics, not yet joined up with the rest of how I see myself.

It has not changed how I live, because no concrete application has landed from it yet.
